input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (acceptable term length) but require one hundred eighty days' advance non-renewal notice. That is double the ninety-day walk-away threshold and well beyond the fallback maximum of sixty days, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term. The pricing limb is satisfied: § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent with ninety days' notice, meeting the preferred position. Redline shortens the window to thirty days and adds the preferred Vendor renewal reminder sixty days before renewal; a sixty-day window remains available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and add a Vendor renewal reminder
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from one hundred eighty days to thirty days and added a Vendor reminder sixty days before renewal, consistent with our position that automatic renewals must be easy to exit. If helpful, we can accept a sixty-day notice window as a fallback.

ops.newText: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice prior to the end of the then-current term. Vendor will notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before the renewal date.
